# Strings

Search, compare, cut up, join and reshape text.

**Library:** [Standard library](index.md#standard-library), for apps and code-pipeline hooks. More in [Cogniscript](../../../concepts/cogniscript.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`StringConcatenate`](#stringconcatenate) | Joins two pieces of text into one. |
| [`StringContains`](#stringcontains) | Whether text contains another piece of text. |
| [`StringEndsWith`](#stringendswith) | Whether text ends with a suffix. |
| [`StringIndexOf`](#stringindexof) | Returns the position of the first occurrence of one piece of text in another, counting from 0, or `-1` when it does not occur. |
| [`StringIsEmpty`](#stringisempty) | Whether text is empty or contains only white space, such as spaces, tabs and line breaks. |
| [`StringJoin`](#stringjoin) | Joins the items of a JSON array into one piece of text, with a separator between them. |
| [`StringLastIndexOf`](#stringlastindexof) | Returns the position of the last occurrence of one piece of text in another, counting from 0, or `-1` when it does not occur. |
| [`StringLength`](#stringlength) | Returns the number of characters in text. |
| [`StringPadLeft`](#stringpadleft) | Pads text on the left to a total length, for example to right-align numbers or add leading zeros. |
| [`StringPadRight`](#stringpadright) | Pads text on the right to a total length, for example to line up columns. |
| [`StringReplace`](#stringreplace) | Replaces every occurrence of one piece of text with another. |
| [`StringSplit`](#stringsplit) | Splits text at every occurrence of a separator and returns the parts as a JSON array of strings. |
| [`StringStartsWith`](#stringstartswith) | Whether text starts with a prefix. |
| [`StringSubstring`](#stringsubstring) | Returns part of text: the characters from a start position, counting from 0, either to the end or for a given length. |
| [`StringToLower`](#stringtolower) | Converts text to lower case. |
| [`StringToUpper`](#stringtoupper) | Converts text to upper case. |
| [`StringTrim`](#stringtrim) | Removes white space, such as spaces, tabs and line breaks, from both ends of text. |
| [`StringUnescape`](#stringunescape) | Turns backslash escapes in text, such as `\n`, `\t` and `\"`, into the characters they stand for. |

### StringConcatenate

Joins two pieces of text into one.

```c
string StringConcatenate(string first, string second)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `first` | `string`, can be empty | The text to put first. |
| `second` | `string`, can be empty | The text to put after it. |

**Returns** `string`: The two joined, with nothing between them.

Unlike `+`, it always joins. `+` adds two values that both read as numbers, so `"1" + "2"` is `3`, while `StringConcatenate("1", "2")` is `12`. Use it when either side might be a number, such as an id or a code.

### StringContains

Whether text contains another piece of text.

```c
bool StringContains(string value, string search, bool ignoreCase)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to search. |
| `search` | `string` | The text to look for. |
| `ignoreCase` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to ignore case; `false` or `""` to match case exactly. |

**Returns** `bool`: `true` when `search` appears in `value`.

The comparison is character by character. Ignoring case does not ignore accents: `é` does not match `E`. Empty `search` text is found in any text.

### StringEndsWith

Whether text ends with a suffix.

```c
bool StringEndsWith(string value, string suffix, bool ignoreCase)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to check. |
| `suffix` | `string` | The text it should end with. |
| `ignoreCase` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to ignore case; `false` or `""` to match case exactly. |

**Returns** `bool`: `true` when `value` ends with `suffix`.

The comparison is character by character. An empty `suffix` matches any text.

### StringIndexOf

Returns the position of the first occurrence of one piece of text in another, counting from 0, or `-1` when it does not occur.

```c
int StringIndexOf(string value, string search, int startIndex, bool ignoreCase)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to search. |
| `search` | `string` | The text to look for. |
| `startIndex` | `int`, can be empty | The position to start searching from. Optional: pass `""` to start at 0. |
| `ignoreCase` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to ignore case; `false` or `""` to match case exactly. |

**Returns** `int`: The position of the first match at or after `startIndex`, or `-1`.

A `startIndex` below 0, or at or past the end of the text, gives `-1` rather than an error, so searching empty text always gives `-1`. Empty `search` text is found at `startIndex`. Positions count the way [`StringLength`](#stringlength) does.

### StringIsEmpty

Whether text is empty or contains only white space, such as spaces, tabs and line breaks.

```c
bool StringIsEmpty(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string`, can be empty | The text to check. |

**Returns** `bool`: `true` when `value` is empty or only white space.

This is the way to test for a missing value. A key [`JsonObjectGet`](json.md#jsonobjectget) did not find, a `null` in JSON and an empty input all read as empty text; no value is ever null, so [`TypeIsNull`](type-checks.md#typeisnull) does not detect them.

### StringJoin

Joins the items of a JSON array into one piece of text, with a separator between them.

```c
string StringJoin(jsonArray array, string separator)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `array` | `jsonArray` | The items to join. An empty value counts as an empty array. |
| `separator` | `string` | The text to put between items, such as `", "`. It can be empty. |

**Returns** `string`: The joined text; empty text for an empty array.

A string item joins as its text, without quotes. Any other item joins as compact JSON, and a `null` as empty text: `["a", 1, {"x":1}, null, true]` joined with `/` gives `a/1/{"x":1}//true`.

### StringLastIndexOf

Returns the position of the last occurrence of one piece of text in another, counting from 0, or `-1` when it does not occur.

```c
int StringLastIndexOf(string value, string search, bool ignoreCase)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to search. |
| `search` | `string` | The text to look for. |
| `ignoreCase` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to ignore case; `false` or `""` to match case exactly. |

**Returns** `int`: The position of the last match, or `-1`.

It always searches the whole text; unlike [`StringIndexOf`](#stringindexof) it has no start position. Empty `search` text gives the length of the text. Positions count the way [`StringLength`](#stringlength) does.

### StringLength

Returns the number of characters in text.

```c
int StringLength(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to measure. |

**Returns** `int`: The number of characters; 0 for empty text.

Most characters count as 1, including accented letters and Arabic, but an emoji and a few rare characters count as 2, because the count is of UTF-16 code units. Positions in [`StringSubstring`](#stringsubstring) and [`StringIndexOf`](#stringindexof) count the same way.

### StringPadLeft

Pads text on the left to a total length, for example to right-align numbers or add leading zeros.

```c
string StringPadLeft(string value, int totalWidth, string paddingChar)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to pad. |
| `totalWidth` | `int` | The length the result should have. |
| `paddingChar` | `string`, can be empty | The character to pad with; only its first character is used. Optional: pass `""` to pad with spaces. |

**Returns** `string`: The padded text.

`StringPadLeft("42", 5, "0")` gives `00042`. Text already as long as `totalWidth`, or longer, comes back unchanged; it is never cut. A negative `totalWidth` raises an error.

### StringPadRight

Pads text on the right to a total length, for example to line up columns.

```c
string StringPadRight(string value, int totalWidth, string paddingChar)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to pad. |
| `totalWidth` | `int` | The length the result should have. |
| `paddingChar` | `string`, can be empty | The character to pad with; only its first character is used. Optional: pass `""` to pad with spaces. |

**Returns** `string`: The padded text.

`StringPadRight("hi", 5, ".")` gives `hi...`. Text already as long as `totalWidth`, or longer, comes back unchanged; it is never cut. A negative `totalWidth` raises an error.

### StringReplace

Replaces every occurrence of one piece of text with another.

```c
string StringReplace(string text, string search, string replace)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | The text to change. |
| `search` | `string` | The text to find. It must not be empty. |
| `replace` | `string` | The text to put in its place. Empty text deletes each occurrence. |

**Returns** `string`: The changed text; text with no occurrences comes back unchanged.

The search is for the exact text, including case; it is not a regular expression. Raises `The value cannot be an empty string. (Parameter 'oldValue')` when `search` is empty.

### StringSplit

Splits text at every occurrence of a separator and returns the parts as a JSON array of strings.

```c
jsonArray StringSplit(string value, string separator, bool removeEmpty)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to split. |
| `separator` | `string` | The text to split at, such as `","` or `"\n"` for lines. |
| `removeEmpty` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to leave out empty parts (from two separators in a row, or one at either end); `false` or `""` to keep them. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The parts, as a JSON array of strings.

`StringSplit("a,b,,c", ",", false)` gives `["a","b","","c"]`, and with `true` for `removeEmpty` it gives `["a","b","c"]`. The separator is matched exactly, including case. The parts are not trimmed: splitting `a, b` at `,` gives `a` and a second part that starts with a space, so split at `", "` or trim each part with [`StringTrim`](#stringtrim).

Splitting empty text gives `[""]`, or `[]` when empty parts are removed. An empty separator does not split: the result is the whole text as one item.

### StringStartsWith

Whether text starts with a prefix.

```c
bool StringStartsWith(string value, string prefix, bool ignoreCase)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to check. |
| `prefix` | `string` | The text it should start with. |
| `ignoreCase` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to ignore case; `false` or `""` to match case exactly. |

**Returns** `bool`: `true` when `value` starts with `prefix`.

The comparison is character by character. An empty `prefix` matches any text.

### StringSubstring

Returns part of text: the characters from a start position, counting from 0, either to the end or for a given length.

```c
string StringSubstring(string value, int startIndex, int length)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to take part of. |
| `startIndex` | `int` | The position of the first character to take, from 0 to the length of the text. |
| `length` | `int`, can be empty | How many characters to take. Optional: pass `""` to take everything to the end. |

**Returns** `string`: The part of the text.

`StringSubstring("hello world", 6, 5)` gives `world`. A length that runs past the end takes what there is, and a start position equal to the length gives empty text. Raises `Start index 4 is out of range for string of length 3` when `startIndex` is negative or past the end, and `Length cannot be negative` for a negative length. Positions count the way [`StringLength`](#stringlength) does.

### StringToLower

Converts text to lower case.

```c
string StringToLower(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to convert. |

**Returns** `string`: The text in lower case.

Letters in any alphabet that has case are converted, not only A to Z. Use `ignoreCase` on the comparison calls, such as [`StringContains`](#stringcontains), rather than lower-casing both sides first.

### StringToUpper

Converts text to upper case.

```c
string StringToUpper(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to convert. |

**Returns** `string`: The text in upper case.

Letters in any alphabet that has case are converted, not only a to z. A letter with no single upper-case form stays as it is: `ß` stays `ß`.

### StringTrim

Removes white space, such as spaces, tabs and line breaks, from both ends of text.

```c
string StringTrim(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to trim. |

**Returns** `string`: The trimmed text.

White space inside the text is kept. Text that is only white space becomes empty text.

### StringUnescape

Turns backslash escapes in text, such as `\n`, `\t` and `\"`, into the characters they stand for.

```c
string StringUnescape(string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | The text to unescape. |

**Returns** `string`: The text with its escapes turned into characters.

Use it on text in which a line break arrived as the two characters `\` and `n`. It handles `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\\`, `\"` and `\u` followed by four hex digits, following .NET's rules for escapes in regular expressions: a backslash before punctuation is dropped (`\.` becomes `.`), and a backslash before a letter that is not an escape raises an error such as `Invalid pattern 'a\qb' at offset 3. Unrecognized escape sequence \q.`

For a JSON string with its surrounding quotes, use [`JsonUnescapeString`](json.md#jsonunescapestring).
